## A Snug alternative with more scheduling flexibility

Snug lets you set the check-in time, and that’s essentially the extent of the customization. CheckinBee offers a bit more: you can set a weekly schedule (for example, check-ins on weekdays only, paused on weekends), adjust the response window — how long the person has to reply before an alert goes out — and set up multiple check-ins per day if that’s needed, each with its own schedule and timing.

For most people, one check-in a day at a consistent time is exactly right. But for those with a more varied routine, or for care professionals managing multiple clients with different needs, the added flexibility matters. [...] But “part of it” is why some people go looking for an alternative. The most common situation: the person who needs the check-in doesn’t have a smartphone, doesn’t want another app to manage, or simply doesn’t want location tracking running in the background of their phone all day. When any of those things are true, Snug runs into a wall.

CheckinBee was built for exactly that gap. The check-ins happen over standard text message — no app to download, nothing to install, no new device to figure out. If the person already knows how to send a text, they already know how to use CheckinBee.

### Both Snug and CheckinBee offer daily safety check-ins for people living alone. But they work quite differently — and the difference often matters a lot to the person being checked in on.

If you’ve landed here, you probably already know what Snug does. It’s a well-regarded service that has helped a lot of families feel less anxious about a parent or loved one living on their own. There’s a real problem it’s trying to solve, and it solves part of it well.

CheckinBee is the most direct competitor to CheckRise in terms of approach — it uses SMS text messages for daily check-ins and does not require a smartphone app. If you liked Snug’s concept but wished it worked via text message, CheckinBee delivers that.

The service has been around for several years and is BBB accredited. The base plan at $13 per month includes a single daily check-in. If you want multiple check-in times per day, the price goes up to $20 per month. [...] The trade-off: CheckinBee has significant reliability concerns. Multiple pages on their website redirect to competitor sites, their blog has not been updated since early 2024, and the pricing and FAQ pages have technical issues. The service appears to still function, but the state of the website raises the same maintenance questions that lead people to look for Snug alternatives in the first place.

CheckinBee also lacks voice call escalation. When a check-in is missed, contacts are notified — but nobody receives an actual phone call. We walk through the website issues and how to run a missed-check-in test before relying on it in our full CheckinBee review.
